**Motivation** — why organisms act and persist — intrinsic and extrinsic motivation, needs, goals and values, the internalization of regulation, and the difference between autonomous and controlled motives; the empirical counterpart of the philosophy of autonomy under `agency` (ADR-023).

| [THEORY-046](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-046.md) v2 | Expected tangible rewards for merely engaging in an interesting task lower later free-choice engagement with it | Deci, Koestner and Ryan (1999, [LIT-557](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-557.md)): across 55 experiments, expected tangible rewards given for working on an interesting task lowered free-choice engagement after the reward stopped (d = −0.40; children −0.43, college students −0.21), and lowered self-reported interest less (−0.15). By their study-by-study account, Cameron and Pierce's rival analysis found the same for this contingency (performance-independent rewards, −0.29), while disputing nearly everything else. Their 2001 reply (LIT-562), read here, re-codes 145 studies and finds it again: rewards offered for doing an interesting task lowered free choice, −0.35 across 57 studies. Active: both sides of the dispute find this effect. | Active |
| [THEORY-047](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-047.md) v2 | A regulation taken in under controlling conditions is introjected rather than integrated, so the social history of how a value was acquired shapes how autonomous acting on it is | Deci and Ryan ([LIT-558](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-558.md)) and Ryan and Deci ([LIT-559](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-559.md)): supports for relatedness and competence are enough to get a value internalized, but only as an introject or a compartmentalized identification; integration also needs autonomy support. The experimental evidence is Deci et al. (1994), as reported: the same amount of internalized behaviour correlated positively with felt freedom and enjoyment under autonomy support and negatively under control. | [THEORY-049](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-049.md) v2 | Whether an external event lowers or raises intrinsic motivation depends on whether it is experienced as controlling or as information about competence | Cognitive evaluation theory, as tested by Deci, Koestner and Ryan (1999, [LIT-557](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-557.md)) and summarized by Ryan and Deci ([LIT-559](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-559.md)) and Deci and Ryan ([LIT-558](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-558.md)): rewards, feedback, deadlines and choice affect intrinsic motivation through their "functional significance". Controlling events shift the perceived locus of causality outward and undermine it; informational ones affirm competence and enhance it, but only with a sense of autonomy. The meta-analytic pattern fits, and controlling versus informational positive feedback differ by d = −0.78 in four studies. Mediation by felt control is untested for rewards. Its rival, Cameron, Banko and Pierce's account (LIT-562), finds rewards tied to a score or to beating others do not undermine. Neither side has tested mediation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-052](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-052.md) v2 | Frustration of the needs for autonomy, competence and relatedness is a transdiagnostic process in psychopathology | Vansteenkiste, Ryan and Soenens (2020, [LIT-561](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-561.md)) propose that need frustration, distinct from mere lack of satisfaction, plays "a transdiagnostic role", citing a longitudinal study in which it predicted adolescents' depressive and eating symptoms and "largely accounted for their co-occurrence". | [THEORY-054](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-054.md) v4 | A regulation is autonomous to the degree it is integrated with one's other values and needs: autonomy is graded, and is not set by the order of the attitude that endorses it | Self-determination theory orders motives on a continuum from external through introjected and identified to integrated regulation and intrinsic motivation. Ryan and Deci ([LIT-559](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-559.md)) and Deci and Ryan ([LIT-558](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-558.md)) place autonomy in integration, "congruence with one's other values and needs", and report a quasi-simplex structure and an experiment in which integrated and introjected internalization behave differently. It is the empirical counterpart of [THEORY-029](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-029.md)'s negative claim. It is not shown that integration can be measured apart from endorsement, and it does not escape Velleman's dilemma. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-067](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-067.md) | Self-control over time needs no faculty of will: interests that dominate at different delays bargain, and resolve is the recursive staking of expected future choices on the present one | Ainslie's précis ([LIT-586](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-586.md)): hyperbolic discounting makes a smaller, sooner reward temporarily preferred, so successive "interests" conflict as in a repeated prisoner's dilemma. Treating a choice as a precedent bundles the series, and summed hyperbolic curves favour the larger, later rewards; a lapse costs credibility. Will is that recursion, not an organ. Schelling ([LIT-602](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-602.md)) describes the same divided chooser from the side of tactics: we manage our later selves as we manage other people. The mathematics of bundling is sound; that willpower works this way is argued, and the précis concedes it is hard to test directly. It is a claim about how control is achieved, not about whose control is self-governance. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-070](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-070.md) | How much cognitive control to exert, and on what, is decided by a cost-benefit computation (the expected value of control) in a specification system distinct from the structures that implement the control | Shenhav, Botvinick & Cohen ([LIT-585](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-585.md)) unify dACC's many reported functions as one: deciding whether, where and how much control to allocate. A control signal has an identity (a task set, a threshold, an attention template) and an intensity; its expected value is its probability-weighted payoff, with future value discounted, minus an intrinsic cost rising with intensity. dACC monitors and specifies; lateral prefrontal and subcortical structures implement. The paper reviews evidence and fits nothing, so Proposed. It does not say what the cost is, how EVC is computed, or that it governs emotion regulation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-077](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-077.md) v2 | Goals pursued for identified or intrinsic reasons receive more sustained effort, which carries their better attainment, and attaining them raises well-being more than attaining goals pursued under pressure | Sheldon & Elliot (1999), [LIT-589](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-589.md): a goal is self-concordant to the degree its reasons are identified or intrinsic rather than external or introjected. | [THEORY-154](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-154.md) | Whether an expected tangible reward lowers or raises later intrinsic motivation depends on how tightly its stated contingency ties it to performance and success | Cameron, Banko and Pierce (2001, [LIT-562](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-562.md)), re-analysing 145 studies with contingencies coded by procedure. | [THEORY-893](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-893.md) v3 | Reward has separable components: 'liking', its hedonic impact, measurable without report by orofacial taste reactivity in humans, apes, monkeys and rodents, and 'wanting', its incentive salience; brain stimulation and sensitization can raise 'wanting' without raising 'liking', so motivation can grow while pleasure stays flat or falls, and 'liking' reactions can occur without any subjective feeling of pleasure | Berridge and Kringelbach (2015), read in [NOTE-1110](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1110.md). | [THEORY-1322](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1322.md) | In Belgian adolescents, need frustration measured by the twelve BPNSFS frustration items statistically absorbs most of the association between depressive and eating disorder symptoms: cross-sectionally their latent correlation falls from .50 to a non-significant .18, and in a two-wave latent change model their correlated change falls from .43 to .24; its mediating role is shown in correlated change over the same six months, not in temporal order | Campbell, Boone, Vansteenkiste and Soenens (2018), [LIT-1964](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1964.md), read in [NOTE-1533](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1533.md) from the early-view PDF on selfdeterminationtheory.org. | [THEORY-1324](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1324.md) v2 | In Ryan, Mims and Koestner's experiment, the same expected reward for doing well left less later free-choice engagement when given with controlling feedback than with informational feedback, and in both styles less than no reward with the same feedback: the interpersonal style of a performance-contingent reward changes its effect, and the reward lowers intrinsic motivation even when the information it carries is held fixed | Ryan, Mims and Koestner (1983), [LIT-1970](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1970.md), read in [NOTE-1522](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1522.md) from the scan on the SDT site. | [THEORY-1325](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1325.md) | In Chirkov et al.'s student samples from South Korea, Russia, Turkey and the USA, the more autonomous people's reasons for engaging in practices of any cultural orientation, collectivist and vertical included, the higher their well-being, with no detectable difference across countries or genders; and vertical practices were much less internalized than horizontal ones | Chirkov, Ryan, Kim and Kaplan (2003), [LIT-1989](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1989.md), read in [NOTE-1513](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1513.md) from the published PDF on selfdeterminationtheory.org. The positive relation held in every country and for every type of practice (β = .15–.42 within country); "no moderation" is twelve non-significant interactions in samples of 94–195. | [THEORY-1326](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1326.md) | In Voigt's model of hard decisions, when two options are valued equally the value differential is too small to choose (conflict, dACC), and the tie is broken during the choice by fixation: precuneus allocates spatial attention bottom-up to the salient item and dlPFC holds it in working memory, which both settles the choice and raises that item's value, a change that lasts only if the choice is remembered (hippocampus) | Voigt (2022), [LIT-1976](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1976.md), an Opinion article read in [NOTE-1517](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1517.md). Proposed. The sharp edge for its use by Jennings ([THEORY-1341](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1341.md)): the attentional step is bottom-up capture by salience, not top-down prefrontal feedback. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1327](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1327.md) v2 | As Ryan and colleagues' 2022 meta-review maps it, the meta-analytic evidence for self-determination theory is concentrated in cognitive evaluation, organismic integration and basic needs theory, is mostly cross-sectional and heterogeneous, and has gaps: no meta-analysis of relationships motivation theory or of need frustration, one or two of causality orientations and goal contents, and none that separates integrated from identified regulation | Ryan, Duineveld, Di Domenico, Ryan, Steward and Bradshaw (2022), [LIT-1967](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1967.md), read in [NOTE-1500](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1500.md) from the accepted manuscript on OSF. | [THEORY-1331](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1331.md) | Deci and Ryan's General Causality Orientations Scale measures autonomy, control and impersonal orientations as three separately scored and largely independent dispositions, reliable and stable over two months, whose validity rests on correlations with self-report measures in small samples, with behaviour its weakest support | Deci and Ryan (1985), [LIT-1955](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1955.md), read in [NOTE-1531](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1531.md) from the scan on the SDT site. | [THEORY-1338](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1338.md) v2 | In the Basic Psychological Need Satisfaction and Frustration Scale as Chen et al. built it, the distinction between satisfaction and frustration coincides with item direction: every satisfaction item states a positive experience and every frustration item an aversive one, so the better fit of six factors over three, which is the scale's evidence that frustration is a separate dimension, is also what a keying or valence factor would produce | Chen et al. Active as a statement about the instrument, checked against its Table 3 item by item and its model comparison (ΔSBSχ²(12) = 450.79, p. 226). | [THEORY-1345](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1345.md) v2 | In three cross-sectional studies of undergraduates, most of the variance in adult attachment security lay within persons, across relational partners (56–79%, error included), and relationship-specific satisfaction of the needs for autonomy, competence and relatedness predicted relationship-specific security in every relationship tested, also with the relatedness items removed; relatedness was the strongest unique predictor, then autonomy, then competence | La Guardia, Ryan, Couchman and Deci (2000), [LIT-1979](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1979.md), read in [NOTE-1523](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1523.md). | [THEORY-1347](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1347.md) v2 | In Patrick, Knee, Canevello and Lonsbary's three correlational studies, perceiving that a romantic partner fulfils one's needs for autonomy, competence and relatedness goes with better relationship quality, with relatedness the strongest unique predictor and the partner's fulfilment adding to one's own; but the measure does not separate the needs, its autonomy and competence subscales correlating .96 once corrected for unreliability | Patrick et al. (2007), [LIT-1971](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1971.md), read in [NOTE-1515](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1515.md) from the article on the SDT site. Active as a careful reading of reported results with their sizes and samples: eight pooled samples (N = 1,918), 66 couples, and 120 diarists with 908 disagreements, all self-report, mostly women students. | [THEORY-1349](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1349.md) | In two cross-lagged panel studies of university students, a negatively worded self-report of need frustration predicted later depressive symptoms (standardized β .13 to .18 over three lags) and later negative affect, net of earlier depression and negative affect, while negative affect did not predict later depression; depression also predicted later need frustration at one lag of two | Levine et al. (2021), [LIT-1974](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1974.md), read in [NOTE-1510](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1510.md) from the version of record in PMC. Active as a statement of the reported paths, checked against Tables 2, 4 and 5. | [THEORY-1573](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1573.md) v2 | Klein and colleagues report that in seventeen labs and 1,550 participants writing about one's own death did not raise preference for a pro-US over an anti-US essay author (g = 0.07, 95% CI −0.03 to 0.17), whether or not the protocol was designed with the original authors | Klein et al. (2022), Many Labs 4, [LIT-1796](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1796.md), read in [NOTE-1322](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1322.md) alongside Chen et al. A preregistered replication of Study 1 of Greenberg et al. (1994; d = 1.34, N = 59), with labs assigned to an author-advised or an in-house protocol. | [THEORY-1577](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1577.md) v2 | Scheffler argues that the survival of other people after one's death is a condition of much of what matters to us mattering, and matters to us in its own right, and reads this as our dependence on future people rather than altruism toward them | Scheffler's 2012 Tanner Lectures, [LIT-1779](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1779.md), read in [NOTE-1298](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1298.md) in place of Death and the Afterlife ([LIT-1754](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1754.md)). | [THEORY-1578](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1578.md) v2 | Stich argues that Sober and Wilson's evolutionary arguments from parental care give no evidence for psychological altruism, the strongest of them failing if hedonism rests on sticky sub-doxastic beliefs, which would make it as reliable as an ultimate desire for the child's welfare, and holds that evolutionary and psychological altruism are logically independent | A critique of Unto Others, read in full in [NOTE-1282](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1282.md). It leaves egoism open, not shown true. Filed from [NOTE-1282](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1282.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-1579](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1579.md) v2 | Syropoulos et al. report that felt responsibility to future generations is endorsed by most people in Europe and the US, is nearly unrelated to ideology and demographics and half as tied to conservatism as responsibility for climate, predicts self-reported proenvironmentalism, and was raised a little by each of five brief interventions, most by a letter to a person born today and least by a longtermist text | Syropoulos et al., thirteen studies and a preregistered experiment (N = 3,175), read in full from the OSF preprint of 2023 without supplements ([NOTE-1293](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1293.md)), in place of Syropoulos and Markowitz 2021; not compared with the published version. | [THEORY-1585](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1585.md) v2 | Kruse and Schmitt, following McAdams, hold that generativity springs from cultural demand and an inner desire that includes a need for symbolic immortality, that its motives can be selfish or altruistic so that it is not altruism, and report, without statistics, that it predicted life satisfaction in older adults and rose in intergenerational projects | Kruse and Schmitt (2012), [LIT-1691](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1691.md), read in [NOTE-1261](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1261.md) in place of McAdams and de St. Aubin (1992). | [THEORY-1591](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1591.md) v2 | Wade-Benzoni, Sondak and Galinsky report that framing an intergenerational decision as leaving burdens rather than using up benefits raised legacy concern, felt responsibility and affinity toward future generations, and that people kept more of a benefit than of a burden for themselves when the other party would receive it in the future, though no study measured legacy concern and allocation together | Wade-Benzoni, Sondak and Galinsky (2010), six small experiments, read in full from the published version ([NOTE-1273](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1273.md)), in place of Wade-Benzoni 2006. Two printed p-values do not match their statistics, one of them the interaction behind Hypothesis 8. | Active |
| [THEORY-1595](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1595.md) v2 | Rubin and Hewstone report, from a count of experiments on social identity theory's self-esteem hypothesis, that intergroup discrimination tends to raise self-esteem but is not in general motivated by low self-esteem, so the hypothesis is not supported in its full and unqualified form, and that most tests measured global personal self-esteem where the theory implies specific social state self-esteem | A qualitative review of over 40 studies, read in full in [NOTE-1278](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1278.md): 18 experiments for and 13 against the first corollary, 7 for and 28 against the second, with no effect sizes. | [THEORY-1599](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1599.md) v2 | Wickersham et al. report that writing about one's legacy, or about a loved place under climate change, raised pro-environmental intentions and hypothetical donations by small amounts that did not differ by age, and that each task raised both legacy motivation and love of nature, which in a model with both mediators carried at least as much of the legacy task's donation effect | Wickersham et al. (2020), 988 American adults sampled evenly by age, read in full with the supplements ([NOTE-1316](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1316.md)), in place of Zaval, Markowitz and Weber 2015, whose legacy task and scale it reuses. The eight-item Legacy Motivation Scale mixes wanting to be remembered with self-regard and felt responsibility to future generations, and only its total is analysed. No condition varies whether anyone will know what one did. | Active |
| [THEORY-1600](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1600.md) v2 | Sandoval-Obando and colleagues report that in 430 Chilean teachers a 14-item Spanish Loyola Generativity Scale has three factors, a three-item Generative Legacy factor on symbolic continuity standing apart from Generative Action (r = .45), from an analysis they call confirmatory that chooses the number of factors from the data | Sandoval-Obando et al. (2026), [LIT-1693](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1693.md), read in [NOTE-1260](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1260.md) in place of McAdams and de St. Aubin (1992). Three factors: Generative Inefficacy (three reverse-coded items, a possible wording factor), Generative Action (eight) and Generative Legacy (three). Exploratory in fact, one convenience sample, no invariance test. | Active |
| [THEORY-1603](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1603.md) v2 | Scheepers and Ellemers present social identity theory: social identity is the part of the self-concept that derives from group membership together with its value and emotional significance, people strive for a positive social identity through favourable comparison with out-groups, and members of low-status groups choose mobility, collective action or social creativity by permeability, legitimacy and stability | A textbook chapter with no new evidence, read in full in [NOTE-1315](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1315.md). Filed from [NOTE-1315](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1315.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-1608](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1608.md) v2 | Spears argues, reviewing the self-categorization account of social influence, that when a group is internalized as a level of self, influence from in-group members is private acceptance and partly self-influence, bounded by shared identity and stronger from more prototypical members, and that crowd members switch to a group identity rather than lose the self | An Annual Review by an author of the SIDE model, read in full in [NOTE-1268](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1268.md). It rereads conformity, obedience, helping, contagion and crowd findings as bounded by shared identity, and cites a meta-analysis of 20 studies in which more prototypical leaders were more influential. Results are reported, not presented. Filed from [NOTE-1268](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1268.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-1609](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1609.md) v2 | Hershfield reviews evidence, mostly from his own studies, that people who feel less similar to their future selves treat them more like strangers and choose less patiently, while directly reported liking and caring for the future self, answered near ceiling, did not predict choice | Hershfield (2011), [LIT-1702](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1702.md), read in [NOTE-1259](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1259.md) from the accepted manuscript. Following Parfit, future self-continuity has three proposed components, similarity, vividness and positivity, each measured or manipulated in studies of saving and discounting. Apart from one r = .47, the review gives no effect sizes. It suggests, untested, that late in life the future self may continue in one's offspring. | Active |
| [THEORY-1615](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1615.md) v2 | Castano, Yzerbyt, Paladino and Sacchi report that in 48 Italian students a reminder of their own death raised identification with Italians, the perceived entitativity of Italians and in-group bias, and propose, without separating it from worldview defence, that a group seen as a real entity lets the self project beyond death | One experiment, read in full in [NOTE-1297](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1297.md). The authors' account of a self extended beyond death is a conjecture they do not test. Filed from [NOTE-1297](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1297.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-1616](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1616.md) v2 | Hurlstone et al. report that in a threshold climate game 9 of 10 groups reached the target when the saved endowment paid the players the next day, 2 of 10 when it paid for trees for future generations, and 7 of 10 when messages meant to activate the legacy motive were added, with no control message and no manipulation check | Hurlstone et al., 30 groups of six, read in full from the publisher's PDF without the supplementary materials ([NOTE-1279](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1279.md)), in place of Wade-Benzoni et al. 2012. The authors call the legacy motive "a mechanism for leveraging short-term self-interest for the long-term best interests of the collective" (p. 9); nothing in the study measures motive. | Active |
| [THEORY-1629](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1629.md) v2 | Chen and colleagues report that the mortality-salience literature, which uncorrected reproduces Burke and colleagues' average effect, shrinks under corrections for publication bias to about r = .18, or to no effect on one method, with true effects so heterogeneous and studies so underpowered that many published effects are likely spurious | Chen, Benjamin, Guo, Lai and Heine (2025), [LIT-1730](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1730.md), read in [NOTE-1271](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1271.md) in place of Burke, Martens and Faucher (2010). 635 effects give g = 0.81 uncorrected (about r = .37); selection models and WAAP-WLS give about r = .18; PET-PEESE finds no positive effect; p-curve finds evidential value at 25% average power; z-curve's expected discovery rate is 8%. | [THEORY-1631](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1631.md) | Sturesteps reports that in 440 Australian adults having a mode of symbolic immortality in one's life, such as children, predicted accepting it as consolation in imagined terminal illness, that accepting the biological, creative and nature modes went with accepting death as final, and that the modes predicted death anxiety and personality only weakly | Sturesteps (1992), [LIT-1689](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1689.md), an ANU master's thesis skimmed in [NOTE-1312](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1312.md) in place of Lifton (1979, [LIT-1714](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1714.md)). It tests Rank's three modes and Lifton's two added ones with vignettes rated as consolation, separating having a mode (availability) from accepting it. Cross-sectional; Rank's sex-difference and neuroticism hypotheses failed. The copy limits copying, so almost nothing is quoted. | Proposed |
